Encode Glycans as Motif Count or Binary Fingerprints

fp_motif_count.Rd

fp_motif_count() counts connected motifs in each glycan. fp_motif_binary() records their presence or absence. By default, both use a fixed built-in dictionary, independent of other glycans in the input batch.

Usage

fp_motif_count(
  glycans,
  ...,
  max_size = 3L,
  motif_dict = "fixed",
  unknown = "ignore",
  na_action = "propagate"
)

fp_motif_binary(
  glycans,
  ...,
  max_size = 3L,
  motif_dict = "fixed",
  unknown = "ignore",
  na_action = "propagate"
)

Arguments

glycans

A glyrepr::glycan_structure() vector or a character vector in any format supported by glyparse::auto_parse(). Formats are detected automatically, as in glymotif. For explicit format selection, use the corresponding glyparse parser first. Structures must be complete: concrete residues, specified linkages, positions, substituents and reducing-end alpha/beta state. Unknown or ambiguous fields raise an error.

...

Reserved for future options. Must be empty.

max_size

Maximum residues per connected motif, an integer from 1 to 7. The default 3 selects all mono-, di- and trisaccharides, including branches.

motif_dict

"fixed" (default) uses the built-in glydb dictionary; "dynamic" builds a dictionary from the non-missing glycans in this call. Dynamic dictionaries may differ across batches, so independently computed vectors cannot be assumed to have aligned coordinates.

unknown

"ignore" (default), "warn" or "error" controls motifs absent from the fixed dictionary. Known motifs are still counted; new coordinates are never added in fixed mode. In dynamic mode, all extracted motifs are included, so this option has no effect. Neither mode permits uncertain input structures.

na_action

"propagate" (default) returns an all-NA vector for each missing input; "error" rejects missing inputs.

Value

A list of named integer vectors, preserving input length, order and names. Motif coordinates are named by canonical structure. Zero and NA entries retain all coordinates. No dictionary object is returned.

Details

The built-in dictionary glydb-2.12.1-complete-v1 contains 24,124 canonical connected motifs of sizes 1–7, derived from 8,211 unique complete structures (8,416 accessions) in glydb's GlyGen 2.12.1 data. The default maximum size 3 selects 3,173 coordinates. Features are sorted by UTF-8 bytes, without hashing or folding. The dictionary does not grow or change with the input batch. Different max_size settings or future dictionary versions define different coordinate sets. Coverage is limited to this source snapshot; unseen motifs follow unknown. See the Get started article for provenance and exclusions.

With motif_dict = "dynamic", each call constructs its own dictionary from all motifs up to max_size in the supplied non-missing structures, including motifs absent from glydb. Unique features are sorted by UTF-8 bytes, so input order and duplicates do not affect the dictionary. Different batches may produce different dictionaries, even at equal vector lengths; combine glycans in one call to ensure aligned dynamic coordinates. Empty input returns list(). An all-missing dynamic batch has no features and returns one named zero-length integer vector per input; retain the original missingness mask because a zero-length vector cannot hold an NA value. A missing input in a mixed batch has all-NA entries for that batch's dynamic dictionary.

Features use glymotif::extract_motif() and glymotif::count_motifs() with substructure alignment, linkages included, strict substituent matching and strict mode. Overlapping occurrences count separately; symmetric mappings of the same residue set count once. Binary values are as.integer(count > 0). Residue identities, linkage labels, substituents and reducing-end alpha/beta information are retained. Protein/lipid attachments and 3D geometry are not represented. Alditols and floating parts/substituents are unsupported.

Complete structures

All fingerprint functions validate complete input structures. Missing inputs are distinct from unknown structure fields: empty input returns list() and missing inputs retain the full coordinate set filled with NA values. Recompute compared vectors when the model, dictionary or implementation changes.

See also

fp_sweetnet(), fp_glycangt(), fp_gifflar()

Examples

a <- "Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1-"
b <- c("Gal(b1-4)GlcNAc(b1-", NA_character_)
fp_a <- fp_motif_count(a)
fp_b <- fp_motif_count(b)
identical(c(fp_a, fp_b), fp_motif_count(c(a, b)))
#> [1] TRUE
fp_a[[1]][c("Gal(b1-", "Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1-")]
#>          Gal(b1- Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1- 
#>                3                2 
lengths(fp_b)
#> [1] 3173 3173
identical(fp_motif_binary(a), lapply(fp_a, \(x) 1L * (x > 0L)))
#> [1] TRUE
dynamic <- fp_motif_count(a, motif_dict = "dynamic")
dynamic[[1]]
#>                   Gal(b1-          Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1- Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1-3)Gal(b1- 
#>                         3                         2                         1
